To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the swelling clay mineral smectite, a common component of Arctic soils, can be transformed into particles of aerosol size and that these particles can form by ice formation in the clay structure.
cryo-TEM images of smectites reveal ice formation within the interlayer and the clay particles are deformed and broken by ice formation.
the freezing process of swelling clays can deform the clay particles and even produce particles with aerosol dimensions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of clay swelling in soil erosion and the formation of aerosols.
understanding how clay structures are deformed by the freezing process and how this deformation may influence the mechanics of soil horizons and soil erosion.
the mechanics of the clay structure in the soil horizons and the effect of freeze–thaw cycles on the soil structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the swelling of clay minerals in the presence of water and the freezing of this water in the pores of the clay structure are the key to the mechanical behaviour of these materials.
the clay minerals in the soil horizons are not only important for the mechanical stability of the soil horisons but also for the formation of aerosol particles that are important for climate.
the cryo-EM data presented here provide a direct and unambiguous link between the structure of smectites, the freezing process and the formation of particles in Arctic soils.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the swelling clay structure is deformed by freezing and the resulting ice crystals can cause the clay particles to fracture into aerosol dimensions.
ice formation can deform and disintegrate clay particles, which can lead to the release of particles into the air and water, and thus contribute to the erosion process.
the clay structure is very sensitive to the freezing process and that the ice formed is very different to that in water ice, and that the ice can be deformed by the swelling clay structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the clay structure is not only a passive component of the soil but also a dynamic and important factor in the erosion of the soil.
the swelling of smectite clay minerals in soils is not a simple process, and that the freezing of water in these soils is not a passive process.
the swelling of clay minerals in the presence of water can produce particles of the size that are important for soil erosion.
